edf6f84bbad537ffffb61dfb0edf6afacf90f8ea: Grindelwald offers 101 km of well-marked runs, a mid-sized ski area that is ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 23 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in peak season. Grindelwald has managed to preserve an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some of the big ski areas. Grindelwald's altitude (1034 m at the base, 2400 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Grindelwald is clearly expensive: 88€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, Grindelwald lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
